text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A poll found that one in every four Swedes would consider working less while taking a cut in pay in order to have more free time.
- Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson says he would consider a multi-billion crown package which would stimulate investments that are good for the environment and create jobs.
- New products and the Internet will generate profits in Ericsson's public telecoms division.
- Volvo board head Bert-Olof Svanholm says the problems at the Swedish vehicle maker are only temporary.
- A missile attack in Denmark on a Hell's Angels party at the weekend which killed two people shows the motorcycle gangs are much better organised than police thought.
- Stora managing director Lars-Ake Helgesson says Stora's profitability is set to increase.
- Some 53 percent of Swedes surveyed believe they could survive financially by running their own businesses compared to 48 percent three years ago.
